findings.F1: The tested relation holds inside the rising profile on the explored folds: the slope of the 5-day return above the coin's drift on the close's place in its 20-day range is 0.0296, with day-clustered t 2.49 (599 non-overlapping cases on 165 days). Closes above the top of the range are followed by +5.17 % above drift (90 cases), against -2.42 % for the lowest band (100 cases).
findings.F2: The relation is carried by calm markets, in and out of the rising profile. Calm is taken as 20-day volatility at or below the coin's median.
findings.F3: Outside the rising profile the relation is also present but weaker. Overall slope is 0.0170, clustered t 1.55 (823 cases). In choppy markets it is 0.0598 with t 2.22 (127 cases, 66 days). In falling markets it is 0.0270 with t 1.59 (401 cases).
findings.F4: The book earns almost entirely on its long side.
findings.F5: In the rising profile, the size of the last day's move relative to volatility predicts the next 5 days (clustered t 2.46, 599 cases). Measured together with the range position, both lose strength: range t 1.82, one-day move t 1.55. It is the same information, not a separate pattern.
findings.F6: Thursday and Friday bars are followed by higher next-day returns: +0.61 % with t 1.93, and +0.55 % with t 2.18 (about 207 days each). This was one of many angles looked at, so it does not stand out from chance and is not used.

ideas.idea: In a calm market, the higher a coin's daily close sits within its 20-day high-to-low range, the more the coin rises over the next 5 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader treats a coin's place in its recent range as a reason to lean its way when the coin has been swinging less than usual, and gives it little weight when the coin is agitated.
ideas.name: calm-market range position drift

ideas.idea: In a rising market, the higher a coin's daily close sits within its 20-day high-to-low range, the more the coin rises over the next 5 days, and the move is largest for closes beyond the top of the range.
ideas.consequence: A trader in a rising coin leans long in proportion to how high the close sits in its recent range, rather than shorting closes low in the range against the market's rise.
ideas.name: rising range-top long drift
